mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 5.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations by lowering discount rates and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% over three months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a contraction in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations fall, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of rising industrial production (INDPRO) above 115, supply chain bottlenecks ease and manufacturing output expands, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 115.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which depresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by rising employment (PAYEMS) above 135,000 thousand, supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 135,000.

mechanism_narrative: In the context of a slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 below 2.0% annualized), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1750 thousand signals a deepening consumer demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 < 2.0% annualized and HOUST < 1750 thousand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 114 and a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.3% indicates a tight labor market supporting manufacturing output, which boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 114 and UNRATE < 4.3%.
